tasks.title: Unit Tests for content-search.js — Fuzzy Search Logic and UI Rendering
tasks.description: public/js/content-search.js (529 lines) is the largest untested client-side module. It powers the keyboard-triggered search overlay (press '/') that indexes all facts, quotes, koans, and section intros. The core logic is pure and testable: normalize() strips HTML and lowercases, scoreMatch() counts query word matches with phrase bonuses, highlightMatch() wraps matches in <mark> tags, truncate() clips text cleanly, and search() orchestrates scoring, sorting, and deduplication. This task creates tests/unit/content-search.test.js with: (1) tests for normalize() with HTML tags, special characters, unicode, and edge cases, (2) tests for scoreMatch() with single words, multi-word phrases, partial matches, and no matches, (3) tests for highlightMatch() verifying correct <mark> wrapping and regex escaping, (4) tests for truncate() at boundary lengths, (5) tests for the full search() pipeline with a mock CONTENT_INDEX, verifying scoring, sorting, deduplication, and the 30-result cap, (6) tests for the DOM rendering functions (createOverlay, performSearch, showOverlay/hideOverlay) using jsdom. Uses vitest + jsdom environment. Effort: 2 sessions.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Create tests/unit/content-search.test.js using vitest jsdom environment. Test pure logic functions (normalize, scoreMatch, highlightMatch, truncate) with fixed inputs. Test search() with a mock CONTENT_INDEX array. Test DOM rendering with jsdom (overlay creation, result rendering, show/hide).
- Test cases: normalize() strips HTML tags, lowercases, collapses whitespace, handles unicode; scoreMatch() returns 0 for no match, 1 per word, +2 bonus for exact phrase; highlightMatch() wraps matches in <mark> with proper regex escaping; truncate() clips at word boundary with ellipsis; search() sorts by score descending, deduplicates by normalized text, caps at 30 results; DOM rendering creates overlay with correct ARIA attributes; performSearch renders grouped results with type labels.
- Integration tests: Verify that the module works with the real content.json and siteData.json structure (index building, search across all content types).
- Acceptance criteria: All new tests pass; >85% branch coverage for content-search.js; existing test suite unaffected; tests run in <10s; no network calls (fully mocked).

tasks.title: Lazy-Load Non-Critical UI Modules (theme-switcher, section-nav, reader-mode)
tasks.description: theme-switcher.js (414 lines), section-nav.js (371 lines), and reader-mode.js (320 lines) are standalone modules loaded via <script> tags in index.astro on every page load, but they are only needed when the user interacts with their respective UI controls. Combined: 1105 lines of JS parsed/evaluated upfront. This task creates a lazy-loader pattern: these modules are loaded as dynamic imports only when the user first clicks their trigger button (theme toggle, nav dot, reader mode toggle). The <script> tags are replaced with small (~20-line) proxy modules that attach click listeners to the trigger elements and dynamically import the full module on first interaction. The flute button, accessibility features, and scene-bundle.js are NOT affected — they load normally. Total added code: ~60 lines across 3 proxy modules. Zero scene-init.js changes.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Test the proxy module logic by mocking dynamic import() and verifying it is NOT called until the trigger element is clicked. Test that subsequent clicks do not re-import (single-load guarantee).
- Integration tests: Verify that the full module loads and initializes correctly after first click. Test that all existing functionality (theme switching, nav scrolling, reader mode toggle) works identically after lazy loading.
- Performance tests: Measure initial JS parse/evaluate time before and after lazy loading; target >100ms reduction on mid-range mobile devices.
- Acceptance criteria: theme-switcher.js, section-nav.js, reader-mode.js are NOT in initial <script> tags; each has a ~20-line proxy module that loads on first click; all existing functionality preserved; dynamic import fires at most once per module; build succeeds; zero scene-init.js changes; total added code ~60 lines.

tasks.title: Automated SVG Optimization for Daily Mutation Assets
tasks.description: The daily-mutate.js script generates SVG visual assets in public/mutation-assets/YYYY-MM-DD/ but never optimizes them. Unnecessary whitespace, comments, metadata, and imprecise path data can bloat SVGs by 30-60%. This task adds an SVG optimization step to the daily mutation pipeline: after an SVG asset is generated, it is passed through svgo (SVG Optimizer) via a scripts/optimize-svg.js wrapper script. The optimizer removes comments, metadata, hidden elements, collapses groups, rounds path coordinates to 2 decimal places, and converts styles to attributes. The optimized SVG replaces the original only if it is smaller (safe fallback). The script is integrated into daily-mutate.js after asset generation and into the daily-deploy.sh pipeline. svgo is added as a devDependency. A --dry-run mode reports savings without modifying files. Effort: 1 session.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Test optimize-svg.js logic with fixture SVGs (unoptimized, already-optimized, malformed) using vi.mock('fs') and vi.mock('child_process') to isolate svgo invocation.
- Test cases: optimized SVG is smaller than original; already-optimized SVG is not rewritten (idempotent); malformed SVG is skipped with a warning (no crash); --dry-run mode reports savings without writing; optimization preserves visual content (key path data retained).
- Integration tests: Run the script against a real unoptimized SVG fixture and verify the output is valid SVG (parsable by DOMParser) and smaller.
- Acceptance criteria: optimize-svg.js exits 0 on valid SVG; exits 0 with warning on malformed SVG; optimized SVGs are ≥20% smaller on average; daily-mutate.js calls optimization after asset generation; svgo added to devDependencies; build succeeds.

tasks.title: Unit Tests for performance-scaler.js — FPS Sampling and Quality Tier Logic
tasks.description: public/js/performance-scaler.js (302 lines) is a standalone module with zero test coverage. It monitors FPS over a rolling window of 60 frames, calculates average FPS, and switches between quality tiers (high/medium/low) with cooldown and hysteresis heuristics. The core logic is pure and testable: given a sequence of frame times, it should compute the correct average FPS, apply the correct quality tier transition, respect cooldown periods, and persist state via sessionStorage. This task creates tests/unit/performance-scaler.test.js with: (1) tests for the FPS calculation logic with synthetic frame time sequences (steady 60fps, steady 20fps, mixed), (2) tests for quality tier threshold detection (below 30fps triggers downgrade, above 50fps for 5s triggers upgrade), (3) tests for cooldown enforcement (no rapid tier flipping), (4) tests for hysteresis (upgrade threshold differs from downgrade threshold), (5) tests for sessionStorage persistence and restoration, (6) tests for the device capability detection (low-end mobile caps at medium quality). Uses vitest with jsdom environment. Effort: 1-2 sessions.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Create tests/unit/performance-scaler.test.js using vitest jsdom environment. Test pure calculation functions (FPS averaging, tier selection, cooldown timing) with synthetic frame time arrays. Mock sessionStorage via jsdom.
- Test cases: FPS calculation returns correct average for steady and variable frame times; quality tier drops to 'low' when avg FPS < 30; quality tier upgrades to 'high' when avg FPS > 50 for 5+ seconds; cooldown prevents tier changes within the cooldown window; hysteresis prevents oscillation (upgrade threshold > downgrade threshold); sessionStorage persists quality tier across page reloads; device capability detection caps low-end devices at medium tier; module gracefully handles missing sessionStorage.
- Integration tests: Verify that the module works correctly when loaded alongside scene-bundle.js by testing the quality tier application.
- Acceptance criteria: All new tests pass; >85% branch coverage for performance-scaler.js; existing test suite unaffected; tests run in <5s; no network calls (fully mocked).

tasks.title: Bundle Size Budget Check in Build Pipeline
tasks.description: The scene-bundle.js (currently ~692KB, includes three.js + all scene modules) has no size guard. Unbounded growth from new 3D features could degrade load times, especially on mobile. This task adds a scripts/check-bundle-size.js script that: (1) reads the built scene-bundle.js file size, (2) compares against configurable thresholds (warn at 750KB, fail at 900KB), (3) outputs a clear PASS/FAIL message with the actual size, and (4) is integrated into the npm run build pipeline between the scene bundle step and the astro build step. The thresholds are configurable via environment variables (BUNDLE_WARN_KB, BUNDLE_FAIL_KB). On failure, the build aborts before the Astro step, saving time. Effort: 1 session.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Test check-bundle-size.js logic with mock file sizes (below warn, between warn and fail, above fail) using vi.mock('fs').
- Integration tests: Run the script against the actual built scene-bundle.js; verify it outputs current size and exits 0 (assuming current size is under threshold).
- Build integration: Modify package.json build script to include the size check between scene bundle and astro build. Verify build succeeds when under threshold.
- Acceptance criteria: check-bundle-size.js exits 0 when bundle < warn threshold, exits 0 with warning when between warn and fail, exits 1 when above fail threshold; npm run build includes the check; thresholds configurable via env vars; build aborts before Astro step on failure.

tasks.title: Content Prefetch — Preload Critical JSON on Idle
tasks.description: After the 3D scene is ready, use requestIdleCallback (with a setTimeout fallback for Safari) to prefetch content.json, siteData.json, and changelog/index.json in the background. These JSON files power client-side features (changelog-app, quote-carousel, moon-phase, content-search) but are currently fetched on-demand, causing a visible delay when panels open. The prefetch module listens for the __sceneReady global event, then fetches and caches all 3 JSON files in a Map. Client-side modules check the cache before fetching. Zero scene-init.js changes — the module is loaded as a standalone public/js/content-prefetch.js script in index.astro. Respects Save-Data header (no prefetch when data saver is on) and respects prefers-reduced-data. Total added code: ~60 lines.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Test the cache Map logic by mocking fetch and verifying cache hits/misses. Test requestIdleCallback fallback with setTimeout.
- Integration tests: Verify that after __sceneReady fires, all 3 JSON files are fetched and stored in cache. Test that subsequent fetches hit cache (no duplicate network requests).
- Acceptance criteria: content-prefetch.js is a standalone module with zero scene-init.js changes; JSON files are prefetched after scene ready; Save-Data header respected (no prefetch); prefers-reduced-data respected; modules can read from cache before fetching; total added code ~60 lines; build succeeds.

tasks.title: Unit Tests for bump-sw-cache.js — Build-Critical Cache Version Increment
tasks.description: scripts/bump-sw-cache.js is a build-critical script that runs on every npm run build. It reads public/sw.js, increments the CACHE_NAME version (e.g., atrija-shell-v3 → v4), and writes the file back. If this script fails silently, the service worker cache never busts, and returning users receive stale HTML/CSS/JS indefinitely. Despite being essential to the cache invalidation strategy, it has zero test coverage. This task creates tests/unit/bump-sw-cache.test.js with: (1) tests that the script correctly increments the version number in CACHE_NAME, (2) tests that it handles the first-run case (no existing version number → defaults to v1), (3) tests that it preserves all other content in sw.js, (4) tests that it handles malformed CACHE_NAME gracefully, (5) tests that the script is idempotent when run twice (v3 → v4 on first run, v4 → v5 on second, no corruption). Uses vitest with vi.mock('fs') for file I/O isolation. Effort: 1 session.
tasks.testingStrategy:
- Unit tests: Create tests/unit/bump-sw-cache.test.js with vi.mock('fs') to isolate all file I/O. Use fixture files in tests/fixtures/sw/ (valid sw.js with CACHE_NAME, sw.js with no version, malformed sw.js).
- Test cases: version increments correctly (v3 → v4, v9 → v10, v99 → v100); first-run case creates v1 from no version; all non-CACHE_NAME content is preserved exactly; malformed CACHE_NAME logs warning and exits gracefully; double-run produces v3 → v4 → v5 (no corruption); script exits 0 on success.
- Integration tests: Run the script against a temporary copy of the real public/sw.js and verify the output is valid JavaScript and the version incremented.
- Acceptance criteria: All new tests pass; >85% branch coverage for bump-sw-cache.js; existing test suite unaffected; mock-based tests run in <5s; no real file system modifications during tests.
tasks.reviewNotes: Reviewed 2026-06-24 06:30 — PASS. 23 unit tests covering version increment, first-run handling, content preservation, malformed input, idempotency, and file I/O. 414-line well-structured test file with vi.mock("fs") isolation. ideas.title: Mobile tulip visibility fix
ideas.description: Tulips were invisible on mobile due to small scale (0.5-0.9), low Y position (-0.5), and narrow aspect ratio. Fixed with larger scale (0.8-1.4), higher Y (-0.1), wider aspect (1.0×1.6).

ideas.title: ASCII moon brightness + shadow

ideas.title: Glitch shader fix
ideas.description: Fix glitch shader R/B channel swap bug (was reading .b for both r and b). Scope chromatic aberration to glitch lines only (~2% per scanline) instead of every frame.

ideas.title: Blue color cast removal
ideas.description: Remove blue point light washing out scene. Change from 0x4466aa to warm 0xffeedd at lower intensity. Reduce post-processing shader saturation from 1.4 to 1.0.

ideas.title: Single-layer flower rendering
ideas.description: Replace 3-layer parallax flower system with proven single-layer approach (a0ce3ef reference). Larger scales, higher Y, correct counts (10 sunflowers, 6 tulips desktop; 6 sunflowers, 3 tulips mobile).

ideas.title: Realistic randomized tulips
ideas.description: Replace abstract oval tulip shapes with realistic cup/bloom forms. 12 non-yellow colors (red, pink, purple, magenta, coral, orange, rose, violet, etc.). Per-tulip randomization: petal count 5-7, width/height variation, curl factor. Petal gradients, edge highlights, vein lines.

ideas.title: Scroll-driven starry night sky parallax
ideas.description: The sky subtly rotates and shifts based on scroll position. Stars at different depths move at different speeds. Moon rises as you scroll. Background color shifts with scroll.

ideas.title: Impressionist brushstroke cursor trail
ideas.description: Custom cursor that leaves painterly brushstroke trails using Canvas 2D particle system. Colors sampled from current theme palette. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

ideas.title: Three.js 3D geometry for all scene elements
ideas.description: Convert all canvas-texture sprites to proper Three.js 3D geometry: sunflowers (TubeGeometry stem + disk + 36 petals in 3 layers), lilies (trumpet petals + 6 stamens with anthers + pistil + spots), music notes (sphere head + cylinder stem + cone flag). Moon upgraded with dual glow spheres. All elements use MeshStandardMaterial with emissive for self-illumination. Billboard heads face camera via lookAt in animate loop.

ideas.title: Code architecture refactoring
ideas.description: Extracted 29KB CSS from BaseLayout to external main.css. Extracted changelog JS and moon-phase JS to external files. Converted 5 duplicated section blocks to data-driven loop. Removed 21 dead files (Three.js component files, shader modules, stale tests). Removed post-processing pipeline (EffectComposer + Glitch shaders). Added modulepreload for Three.js CDN. HTML inline CSS reduced from 45KB to 2KB.

ideas.title: 3D Cypress Tree Silhouettes
ideas.description: Tall, dark cypress tree silhouettes rendered as Three.js ExtrudeGeometry that sway gently in the background. 5 trees on desktop, 2 on mobile. MeshBasicMaterial for zero lighting cost. Integrates with existing parallax scroll system.

ideas.title: Interactive Firefly Swarm
ideas.description: A swarm of 3D firefly points (40 desktop, 20 mobile) that drift organically using damped random walk velocity fields. Each firefly pulses with warm golden light via custom shader. Fireflies scatter away from mouse cursor within 3-unit radius and slowly return. Additive blending for ethereal glow.

ideas.title: Scroll-Driven Painting Reveal
ideas.description: A large painting (loaded from Wikimedia Commons) displayed on a Three.js PlaneGeometry that progressively reveals based on scroll position. Custom shader divides the image into horizontal bands with slight horizontal variation for organic reveal. 150vh scroll section drives the effect.

ideas.title: Theme Color Scheme Switcher
ideas.description: A floating theme picker that lets visitors manually switch between the 5 impressionist color schemes (starry-night, sunflower, midnight-wave, tulip-garden, moonlit-silver). Orphaned PRD from earlier generation — needs review before implementation.

ideas.title: Dynamic Time-of-Day Atmosphere System
ideas.description: The 3D scene subtly shifts its ambient atmosphere based on the visitor's local time — warm golden dawn, bright midday, rich sunset tones, or deep night. Background, stars, moon, waves, and flower colors all respond to time-of-day with smooth interpolation between phases.

ideas.title: Impressionist Visitor Guestbook
ideas.description: A lightweight, localStorage-backed guestbook where visitors leave short impressions (max 140 chars) that appear as floating, brushstroke-styled text sprites in the 3D scene. Entries persist across visits. No backend — purely client-side.
ideas.deferredReason: localStorage-only impressions have no persistent value. Deferred until backend option exists.

ideas.title: Wind-Swept Wheat Field
ideas.description: A field of golden wheat stalks rendered as InstancedMesh in the lower 3D scene, swaying organically in a procedural wind vertex shader. 800 stalks desktop / 300 mobile. Scroll position modulates wind intensity.

ideas.title: Particle Poetry Scroll Effect
ideas.description: As visitors scroll through content sections, key words from headings and intros emerge as 3D CanvasTexture sprites that float upward and fade. Each section has a themed word pool. 25 sprites desktop / 12 mobile. Purely visual — no audio.

ideas.title: Seasonal Scene Transitions
ideas.description: The 3D scene's color palette, flower emphasis, and atmospheric tone shift based on the current calendar season (spring/summer/autumn/winter). Implemented as a content/data layer — daily-mutate.js uses weighted seasonal selection for color schemes and flower ratios. No scene-init.js changes.

ideas.title: Light Mode — prefers-color-scheme Support
ideas.description: Respect the user's OS-level color scheme preference by providing a light/cream impressionist palette activated via @media (prefers-color-scheme: light). The light mode uses warm cream (#faf6f0) backgrounds, dark brown (#2a1f14) text, and softened gold accents — evoking sunlit canvas rather than night sky. All color values are CSS custom property overrides under the media query, so zero JS is required. The existing 3D scene remains unchanged (it's a dark sky scene). Text content, cards, navigation, and the loader all adapt. Enhances accessibility for users who experience eye strain in dark environments or simply prefer light themes.
